en: The sampaguita, chosen as the national flower in 1934, gets its name from the Chinese phrase "sekampuit," meaning "I promise you."
The Philippine flag is unique because it is flown with the red stripe on top during wartime and the blue stripe on top during peacetime.
The Philippine Supreme Court has exactly fifteen justices who hold the exclusive power to declare any legislative or executive act unconstitutional.
Carved by the Ifugao people over two thousand years ago, the Banaue Rice Terraces feature an ancient stone-wall irrigation system that still channels mountain springs through every level.
In the ancient Baybayin writing system, every consonant inherently includes an "a" vowel sound unless a small mark called a kudlit is added.
Jose Rizal secretly adopted the surname "Rizal" to avoid Spanish suspicion, as his brother's connection to an executed priest made their original surname heavily monitored.
Known as the "Mother of All Philippine Festivals," Ati-Atihan participants paint their faces black to honor the indigenous Ati people who welcomed early Malay settlers.
The 1987 Constitution lowered the national voting age from twenty-one to eighteen, instantly granting millions of young Filipinos the right to elect their leaders.
Dr. Fe del Mundo invented a bamboo incubator using native baskets and hot water bottles, providing a life-saving, low-cost alternative for premature babies in rural hospitals.
To join the secret Katipunan society, Andres Bonifacio required new members to sign their application papers with their own blood drawn from their left arm.
The core Filipino value of bayanihan originally involved an entire community physically carrying a traditional nipa hut on bamboo poles to relocate it for a neighbor.
Juan Luna’s masterpiece "Spoliarium" won the first gold medal at the 1884 Madrid Exposition of Fine Arts, measuring an enormous four meters tall and seven meters wide.
